description: We are Callisto Destino, a team from Eyuboglu Science and Technology High School. Our mission is to integrate our scientific expertise with our technological skills to contribute to the future of space and further exploration. Our team’s interests and skills include game design and developing engaging gameplay experiences.
summary:
Our game brings real NASA missions to life by turning them into interactive challenges. Players can experience what it is like to be astronauts aboard a spacecraft while carrying out various activities, including adjusting gyroscopes, conducting biological experiments in space, also maintaining equipment and gathering scientific information. Through these activities, the game aims to introduce space exploration in an entertaining and engaging way.
We created our game with Scratch, a block-based coding platform that enables users to develop games and animations. Using this platform, we built the spacecraft setting, designed different mission scenarios, and coded the interactions, movements, and behaviours of various objects.
details:
Callisto Explora is a game that aims to help the players gain a wider perspective of, improve their knowledge on and make it easier to visualise what space missions actually entail. This is achieved by letting them take on the roles of astronauts aboard a spacecraft to complete tasks and face challenges inspired by NASA’s past space missions. We intend to make space exploration more accessible to a wider audience, especially younger generations, and encourage curiosity towards space and science from an early age. When they first enter the game, the players are faced with a starting menu with the game logo and two buttons under it. The options button in the menu lets them adjust the volume of the background music and choose a character to represent them in the game before starting. The three character choices are different animals(chimpanzee Ham, cat Félicette and dog Laika) who have become prominent figures in the history of space exploration by being sent to space to study the effects of space travel on living organisms. The start game button takes the player to a screen that lets them design a space shuttle to launch. The “Biological Sample Collection” mission draws on NASA’s real experiments growing radishes aboard the International Space Station (ISS). It turns the scientific challenge of growing plants in microgravity into an interactive space mission, letting players experience growing food in space and explore the possibilities for sustainable life on future missions.In the “Robotic Arm Asteroid Collection” mission, players operate a robotic arm aboard a spacecraft to collect asteroid samples. The robotic arm is used to carefully approach, grab, and secure asteroid material for further scientific investigation. The mission is inspired by real NASA asteroid exploration projects, such as OSIRIS-REx, which collected samples from the asteroid Bennu. Its purpose is to introduce players to robotic technology, asteroid research, and the challenges of collecting materials in space.

The game was made with Scratch using block-based coding. All the visuals used are original drawings.

Since the game is intended to help people with little to no idea about space exploration missions, our team decided that our target audience would be on the younger side. This made us prioritize comprehensible game mechanics and engaging visuals over extensive technical information. We also took care to include various missions to introduce players to different aspects of space exploration.
